ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: This is a food web diagram. The resource/producer label at the bottom says "Cladophora, epiphytic diatoms, Nostoc". From this bottom label, there is an arrow directly pointing to "Tuft-weaving chironomids". The picture also shows Tuft-weaving chironomids then connected by arrows to other organisms, such as predatory insects, roach fry, stickleback fry, etc. Reasoning: The question asks what might happen immediately if Cladophora died. In the food web, arrows point from resources to the organisms that depend on them, so the organism directly dependent on bottom resources such as Cladophora is Tuft-weaving chironomids. If Cladophora dies, the most directly and immediately affected would be Tuft-weaving chironomids, which might die or become extinct because of losing their food source.
